stem: In a sample space of ${=total}$ equally likely outcomes, $n(A) = {=na}$, $n(B) = {=nb}$ and $n(A \cap B) = {=nab}$. Find $P(A \cup B)$.
solution: The addition rule: $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$.
The overlap is counted twice if it is not subtracted: $n(A \cup B) = {=na} + {=nb} - {=nab} = {=nunion}$.
notes: Reproduces the hand-written family tpl:t2u3-1-3:union in generate_questions.py, item for item (decision 16 proof, tests/test_family_reproduction.py). Misconception ids are the catalogue's (seed/generated/misconceptions.json), which the live bank carries. Not loaded by anything: the live Prep-3 bank is the committed export.
